chunks: Ali ibn mahboub from Is'haq ibn Ammar who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'My father (peace be upon him) was saying: We seek Refuge with Allah from the sins which hasten annihilation, bring death closer, and vacate the households, and they are cutting off of relationships, ingratitude, and neglect of righteousness.'
ai.seo_question: What are the three sins that hasten death and empty households according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrates from his father, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him), a supplication seeking refuge in Allah from specific sins that cause premature death and empty homes. These sins are identified as severing family ties (qati'at al-rahim), disobedience to parents (al-uquq), and neglecting righteousness (turk al-birr). This narration highlights the causal link between moral decay, particularly in kinship, and physical destruction, a theme emphasized in Shia exegesis where 'emptying dwellings' refers to the loss of inhabitants due to divine punishment.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘My<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘We<sup>asws</sup> see Refuge with Allah<sup>azwj</sup> from the sins which hastens the annihilation brings the death closer, and vacates the households are the cutting off of relationships and the ingratitude (to the parents), and the neglect of the righteousness’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn Mahbub from Ishaq ibn ‘ Ammar who has said the following:

“I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) saying, ‘My father would say, “We seek refuge in Allah against the sin that hastens one’s perishing, draws death closer, and vacates the towns. Such sins are failing to maintain good relations with relatives, failing to maintain good relations with parents and disregarding virtuous deeds.’”
